Definition: from κόλλα ("glue"); to glue, i.e. (passively or reflexively) to stick (figuratively):--cleave, join (self), keep company.
BiblicalUsage: Kollao means to glue, to cleave, to join oneself. Matthew 19:5 says a man shall leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife, and they twain shall be one flesh, Luke 15:15 has the prodigal joining himself to a citizen of that country, and being sent to feed swine, and 1 Corinthians 6:17 says, he that is joined unto the Lord is one spirit.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe three joinings make the whole moral map: cleave to a wife, join yourself to a citizen and feed swine, or be joined to the Lord and be one spirit.
